 Liga MX América vs Toluca: the forgotten final of 110,000 that changed Mexican soccer forever
 Alejandro Reza twitter Calum Roche twitter Update: Oct 30th, 2026 04:00 EDT 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google América and Toluca will face off this Saturday, October 31, at Estadio Banorte in a Matchday 15 clash in the Apertura 2026 tournament. Kickoff is scheduled for 11:10 p.m. ET (9:10 p.m. local time).
 The meeting also offers an opportunity to revisit one of the most significant chapters in the history of both clubs: the first-ever Mexican soccer Liguilla final , contested by the Águilas and the Diablos Rojos during the 1970-71 season.
 The first Liguilla final between América and Toluca
 The historic championship series brought together América, who finished top of the regular-season standings, and second-place Toluca . Their meeting marked the beginning of a new era in Mexican soccer, with the league title decided through a playoff format.
 The first leg took place on July 25, 1971, at Estadio Nemesio Diez, Toluca’s home stadium. The two teams played out a tightly contested encounter that ended in a goalless draw.
 América claimed the title at Estadio Azteca
 The return leg was played on August 1, 1971, at Estadio Azteca, in front of approximately 110,000 fans. With the championship on the line, América made the most of home advantage to secure the trophy.
 The Águilas won the second leg 2-0, sealing a 2-0 aggregate victory and becoming the first champions crowned under the new Liguilla format.
 Horacio López Salgado and Carlos Reinoso made history
 América’s goals came from Horacio López Salgado and Carlos Reinoso , whose contributions proved decisive in securing victory over Toluca. Their strikes became part of a landmark final in Mexican soccer history.
 On the Toluca bench was Ignacio “Nacho” Trelles, one of the most celebrated coaches in Mexican soccer history. Despite his considerable experience, he was unable to prevent his side from falling to the Águilas.
 América secured their second league championship
 The victory over Toluca delivered the second league title in América’s professional history , establishing that championship series as a defining moment for future generations of players and supporters.
 More than five decades later, the two clubs will meet again in the Apertura 2026, this time in Matchday 15. Although there is no trophy directly at stake, América and Toluca will both be looking to collect valuable points as the regular season approaches its conclusion.
